I like usually like weird / disturbing / difficult / RPGMaker / indie type games, so I really thought I'd like this one given the amount of positive reviews and the hype around how emotionally brutal this game is. 

But it's just not good; not the gameplay, not the story, really not much of it. I'm honestly a bit baffled by all the praise for this game. Except the soundtrack. The soundtrack is amazing. 

Artistically speaking, the story has an interesting setup, and the world is kind of interesting in a bizarrely grim and quirky way, but it doesn't really go anywhere interesting. The characters especially feel like caricatures and lack any sort of emotional depth or complexity. All those video essays talk about how the game explores abuse, trauma, grief, regret, etc. but it really doesn't, at least not substantially. It just shows you a bunch of that stuff happening and kinda leaves it at the surface level. I didn't find any emotional impact or believability in anything that I saw (again, except maybe the very beginning with Brad raising Buddy and her disappearing), and I don't really see how people extract anything profound from it. It's like how if a horror movie shows you a bunch of scary or gory stuff, people may respond to the shock impact of what they are seeing but that stuff alone doesn't make a good movie. 

And as for the gameplay, there are many sections that are tedious and kinda inexcusable from a design perspective. The driving sections, the pseudo-platforming that punishes you for making a wrong jump, dead-ends and time wasters. The combat at least I thought was sufficiently challenging at first, but it doesn't take long to find workarounds and strategies that make it a bit too easy. 

But WOAH, then the game BRUTALLY FORCES you to LOSE TEAMMATES, pretty gruesome huh? But no. Firstly there is an excess of party members, so the worst thing about losing some is that you have to grind up your replacements (more tediousness). And secondly, if the main characters are shallow, the recruitable side characters are even moreso. How could I possibly get attached to or care about these characters dying in ways that the game pushes on me nonsensically in an attempt to make me FEEL THE PAIN? 

And I think maybe what ties all these weaknesses together, and I've seen mentioned in other negative reviews is the weirdly inconsistent emotional tone the game has. It's like it tries to be funny and absurd, but also super dark and emotionally serious, but fails at both. The absurd parts are at least memorable... I can say that much. But what kind of world is this? There is nowhere near enough emotional depth, or maybe just raw believable humanity? for the dark parts to actually be disturbing (like Fear & Hunger), OR for the funny parts to actually be endearing (like Earthbound or Undertale). I dunno, it comes across like a bad cartoon or something. 

So despite having high hopes for this game, it failed on all fronts for me. I don't think the praise is warranted. There is genuine creativity on display here for sure, and I will praise the soundtrack endlessly. But overwhelmingly positive? I just don't see it

More Undertale than Undertale ever was. Every time I've come back to this, I keep getting the same feeling, even if that was never Dingaling's idea. Undertale just appeals to easier to stomach themes, leaving this much more cutting narrative to never quite reach as far as I wish it could.

What I mean by that is the whole choices matter thing. You get some devastatingly morbid choices to make, all contained in a man so utterly tragic that any amount of pain and suffering he has to endure feels completely justified, not just for his actions but also inactions and guilt. Everything sucks in a special way that makes you desperately want to give someone a hug and give them, for however fleeting a moment, a little bit of solace in a world filled with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiots.

And yes, it is also a funny game. Pitch black humor, but still funny. People with weird abilities, or getting kicked in the nuts, falling on your face from fourty feet up or some other dumb things.

It's a cruel game, you will rage more times than you'd care for because of how it likes to ♥♥♥♥ you over, but the journey is worth every moment. A solid entry to, and likely one of the first "earthbound inspired RPGS about depression." If you like the genre, you'd be fool to pass it up.

This is by far one of the most innovative and strategic turn-based experiences I have ever had. There's a compelling and memorable story that works WITH the gameplay and combat elements. I have enjoyed this genre since FF Tactics came out and I can promise you that NO other game keeps you on your toes than LISA. Feels like a rollercoaster the entire time you play. The way LISA has you gamble with the lives of your party and resources, which can have PERMANANT repercussions on your playthrough, keeps the stakes high. The monetary system (dirty mags) is balanced so well as to make store purchases important, among other elements I won't spoil which also make purchases FEEL strategic. 

The visual elements are simplistic and are skillfully used with the comedy. LISA the Painful is a master of comedic timing and accomplishing a compelling narrative with just a few pixels. The visual style (although some of the comedy doesn't) is continued in LISA the Joyful.

I will also make a criticism of LISA the Joyful (which I hear was a stretch goal from the initial project anyway) for having a too simplistic combat style compared to what came before it. The lore additions were mostly unnecessary and only served to pull some of the mystery away from Painful. I am absolutely still glad it exists, but would consider it an extra chapter to tie up loose ends rather than a sequel.

Thanks for giving me something to look forward to at the end of the day, LISA.

A formative experience that I will never recover from or forget for as long as I live. While I am not a fan of the definitive edition changes, the legacy version still holds up well and regardless of the game version you will not have a bad time (I think...).

There's not a ton I can say about this game without spoilers I feel, but it's a game with a very good story and a rewarding system once you get the hang of how it works. The music, too, is something they should be quite proud of! In terms of RPGs, it's one I'll be recommending when someone asks me for a suggestion.

After playing through the base game to your hearts content, I strongly suggest giving the DLC (Lisa: The Joyful) the same treatment as it ties up the story of our main characters in a neat little bow. I'd love to see more of this world one day, possibly from another perspective.

I wish I could say more, but what I can offer is this: Sometimes taking the tougher road gives the most rewarding outcome. Don't give up, you've got this. ♥
